With over $11 billion in [assets under management](https://www.fool.com/terms/a/aum/), the **First Trust Nasdaq Cybersecurity ETF** ( [CIBR](https://www.fool.com/quote/tsx/cibr/) +2.78%) is by far the largest pure-play ETF in this part of the [technology sector](https://www.fool.com/investing/stock-market/market-sectors/information-technology/). This large financial services firm offers a variety of investment products, and its cybersecurity offering is one of the longest-tenured in the ETF world. Its inception dates back to 2015, and the fund's shares have more than tripled since then.

The First Trust Cybersecurity ETF currently comprises 32 cybersecurity companies, almost all of which are listed on a U.S. stock exchange. A handful of stocks are in adjacent industries, such as aerospace and defense, where security services are prominently featured.

At the time of this writing, the top three holdings (which comprise about 24% of the fund's assets) are large tech companies **Broadcom** ( [**NASDAQ:AVGO**](https://www.fool.com/quote/nasdaq/avgo/) **), Palo Alto Networks (** [NASDAQ: PANW](https://www.fool.com/quote/nasdaq/panw/)), and **Cisco Systems Inc.** ( [CSCO](https://www.fool.com/quote/nasdaq/csco/) +3.94%). The ETF is rebalanced quarterly and has an annual [expense ratio](https://www.fool.com/terms/e/expense-ratio/) of 0.58% ($5.80 in fees are deducted from the fund's performance each year for every $1,000 invested).

The Global X Cybersecurity ETF (BUG) seeks to invest in companies that stand to potentially benefit from the increased adoption of cybersecurity technology, such as those whose principal business is in the development and management of security protocols preventing intrusion and attacks to systems, networks, applications, computers, and mobile devices.

## ETF Objective
The Global X Cybersecurity ETF (BUG) seeks to provide investment results that correspond generally to the price and yield performance, before fees and expenses, of the Indxx Cybersecurity Index.

## ETF Details
### [HACK](https://www.sumgrowth.com/etf-profile/invest-in-HACK-etf.html) - Amplify Cybersecurity ETF
The ETFMG Prime Cyber Security ETF (HACK) is designed to provide investors with exposure to companies that are leaders in the cybersecurity industry. The fund seeks to track the Prime Cyber Defense Index, which includes companies involved in developing and managing security protocols to prevent intrusion and attacks on systems, networks, applications, computers, and mobile devices. HACK offers a diversified portfolio of global cybersecurity firms, ranging from large-cap to small-cap companies, ensuring broad exposure to this critical and rapidly growing sector. As cyber threats continue to escalate, HACK provides investors with a way to capitalize on the increasing demand for cybersecurity solutions.

### [WCBR](https://www.sumgrowth.com/etf-profile/invest-in-WCBR-etf.html) - WisdomTree Cybersecurity Fund
The fund is rebalanced annually to ensure alignment with its index methodology.

### [CIBR](https://www.sumgrowth.com/etf-profile/invest-in-CIBR-etf.html) - First Trust NASDAQ Cybersecurity ETF
The First Trust NASDAQ Cybersecurity ETF (CIBR) is an exchange-traded fund that seeks to track the performance of the NASDAQ CTA Cybersecurity Index. This index is designed to measure the performance of companies engaged in the cybersecurity segment of the technology and industrials sectors. CIBR provides investors with exposure to firms that develop, manufacture, or distribute cybersecurity hardware, software, or services. The fund is passively managed and employs a full replication strategy to mirror the index's holdings. Cybersecurity is a critical and rapidly growing industry, driven by increasing digital threats and regulatory requirements for data protection. CIBR offers a diversified approach to investing in this high-growth sector, with holdings spanning large-cap, mid-cap, and small-cap companies globally.

### [BUG](https://www.sumgrowth.com/etf-profile/invest-in-BUG-etf.html) - Global X Cybersecurity ETF
The Global X Cybersecurity ETF (BUG) seeks to invest in companies that stand to benefit from the increased adoption of cybersecurity technology. This includes companies involved in the development and management of security protocols preventing intrusion and attacks to systems, networks, applications, computers, and mobile devices. The fund provides exposure to a broad range of cybersecurity firms, from established leaders to emerging players, offering investors a way to capitalize on the growing importance of digital security in an increasingly connected world. BUG tracks the Indxx Cybersecurity Index, which is designed to measure the performance of companies that are primarily involved in cybersecurity activities, including hardware, software, and services.
